extracted.intended_audience: readers and practitioners of Canadian policing history; police officers and administrators; general readers interested in Royal North‑West Mounted Police
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and desiderata for the Royal North‑West Mounted Police as described in a historical narrative — i.e., the qualities, practices and duties by which the Force is judged and organized. Focuses on operational conduct, recruitment/promotion, investigative methods, civil assistance and public order roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness / 'played fair'
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct marked by fair dealing; when a man 'played fair' nothing unusual was suspected and things resumed their even tenor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit standard for policing behaviour: fair, open dealings reduce suspicion and maintain public confidence; contrasted with deceptive or unfair conduct which arouses suspicion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness in criminal capture
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Certain and deadly precision of the Mounted Police methods in relation to the capture of criminals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by successful apprehension of offenders (examples: capture and conviction of Fisk and Robertson) and by investigations leading to confessions and convictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence and dogged determination in investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must show endless patience and doggedness (e.g., Sergeant Hetherington searched hotel registers and mining districts for three months using letter‑formation clues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued investigative virtues: long‑term follow‑up, painstaking comparison of evidence, willingness to travel and work continuously until a suspect is located.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forensic and observational detective methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of small physical clues and comparative techniques (e.g., buckle indicating Kalamazoo, handwriting/letter‑formation comparison) to identify victims and suspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages creative, meticulous use of material evidence and records (hotel registers, pay rolls) and careful handwriting analysis as valid investigative tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogation leading to confession
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactical interviewing (e.g., Duffus taking Robertson aside, warning him and inviting statement) resulting in full confession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows authorized, methodical interrogation can produce admissions; implies need for proper procedure (coroner's permission) and controlled environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint in the use of force
rubrics_metrics.description: Mounted Police 'preserved their reputation for refraining from taking the aggressive until there was no other course open' (drew revolvers only when men were in danger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of force as last resort; maintain restraint and only escalate when necessary to protect officers or public (example: Winnipeg strike control where weapons were displayed only after danger to men).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting life, property and essential services
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty to protect life and property and ensure public services (e.g., carrying and distribution of mails during strikes, rescue in Regina cyclone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational priority: prevent interruption of essential services and safeguard civilians; active intervention in emergencies and civil disturbances when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tact and firmness in community relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tact and firmness used to establish order (e.g., Constantine's tact and firmness in Yukon; policing labour camps on Hudson's Bay Railway).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance courteous cooperation with decisive action; tact to gain local cooperation, firmness to enforce law — praised as creating orderly communities and facilitating projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality / impartiality in disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: 'While never taking part with either employer or employed, the firm, impartial and tactful Mounted Police Force often became a living windbreak against social tempests.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Police must be impartial arbiters in labor and local disputes, enforcing law without favoring parties; impartiality helps maintain public trust and prevents escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: High recruitment and personnel standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner aimed to accept recruits on probation, discharge those lacking 'energy, intelligence and character,' and make dismissal the severest punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes selective recruitment, probationary periods, and strict disciplinary standards to improve personnel quality and maintain a high‑calibre force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit‑based promotion and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotions and honors given in recognition of service and merit (e.g., inspectors promoted, surgeons made honorary, awards for conspicuous bravery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career advancement tied to demonstrated competence, experience and heroism; public recognition reinforces standards and esprit de corps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readiness and rapid civil assistance in emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Whole resources of the Mounted Police placed at city's disposal during Regina cyclone; officers worked continuously to rescue injured and secure property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations: mobilize quickly in disaster, provide rescue and security, and sustain operations until civil order restored; seen as civic duty beyond policing crimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valour and courageous conduct in peacetime
rubrics_metrics.description: Peace‑time acts of gallantry (e.g., Constable Moorehead entering a high‑pressure gas station to save men) should be recognized and rewarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bravery in non‑combat situations is a high ideal; argument for decorations recognizing peacetime heroism up to the level of wartime honors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patrol oversight and effective presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular oversight by patrols in remote districts (Hudson's Bay, Mackenzie, Yukon) carried out without untoward incident; the mere presence of the Force conferred order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importance of patrols for crime prevention, local oversight and as a visible deterrent; consistent patrols foster safety and orderly development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivity and fair adjudication with Indigenous peoples and traders
rubrics_metrics.description: Tact and friendly dealing with natives and traders introduced a new code of ethics in the Northland; patrolmen became 'recognized as fair and impartial adjudicators.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective northern policing requires respect, cultural understanding and fairness in small disputes (sled‑dog ownership, fur exchanges); these practices inculcate property rights and respect for life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endurance and capability in harsh conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to undertake long, arduous patrols (e.g., fifty‑two days and over 1,000 miles; reliance on dog teams) and to operate in lonely, extreme climates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical stamina, skill with transport (horses, dog teams), and psychological resilience are required for northern/arctic duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with other government departments and duties protecting federal interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Force must investigate loss or misappropriation of Federal property, assist Customs to prevent smuggling, help Inland Revenue against illicit liquor, cooperate with Indian Affairs and Agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad federal policing responsibilities demand interdepartmental cooperation and adaptability to varied statutory duties beyond ordinary criminal law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational adaptability and proper jurisdictional alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension of jurisdiction from North‑West to whole of Canada and absorption of Dominion Police to avoid duplication; moving headquarters to Ottawa to match nationwide remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative reforms should align structure with operational needs; jurisdictional clarity and consolidation improve national policing efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention and suppression of sedition and revolutionist activity
rubrics_metrics.description: During wartime, the Force monitored and suppressed pro‑enemy or revolutionary agitation among alien elements and radical movements (e.g., Winnipeg strike leaders with seditious aims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic security role includes intelligence, monitoring of subversive organisations, and enforcement actions that balance civil liberties with national safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation, reporting and recognition of otherwise unnoticed heroism
rubrics_metrics.description: Many deeds of heroism noted tersely in reports; reports reveal danger and bravery 'between the lines' (example: Constable Wight's arrest of man with dynamite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough reporting preserves record of service, supports recognition and promotes institutional memory; encourages accurate, candid detachment reports.
